say: Be found on Google, get reviews, and track what really sells.
This is the video for module two: search, local visibility and analytics.
A customer who searches is already looking for what you sell. That is the warmest customer you can get.
Google does not search the whole internet at that moment. Its programs follow links and discover pages in advance.

say: Halima runs a salon in Kano. She sent her review link to 48 happy clients. About 1 in 4 left a review, taking her from 4 to 16.
One client gave 2 stars after waiting 40 minutes. Halima thanked her, apologised, and explained that she now confirms times the evening before.

panel.heading: Halima's reviews: honest asking works
left: Send your review link after service
Fix the problem a review names

say: Never fake, buy or pay for reviews. Google's rules forbid it, and it can remove reviews or restrict your profile.

say: Ngozi sells skincare and added UTM labels to her Easter links, so Google Analytics could see where each visitor came from. Instagram brought 600 visits and 12 purchases.
WhatsApp brought only 150 visits, but 9 purchases. That is 6%, three times better.
Email converted at 4%. So she grows her WhatsApp list, with permission, and keeps Instagram for awareness. Watch orders, not likes.
No website? Ask every new customer, how did you hear about us, and record it. Each Monday, fill in one row for last week, and write one decision to test.
Keep the sheet private, because names and phone numbers are personal data.

say: To remember. Use the local phrases your customers type. Complete your Google profile, and ask honestly for reviews.
Keep cost per order below your profit per sale. And measure messages and orders, not likes.
